speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where your neck and arm pain is located, and does it radiate down a specific path to your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness or numbness follow a specific dermatomal pattern, such as affecting only the thumb and index finger, or is it more generalized across the entire hand? I also need to know if you have noticed any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or writing.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the presence of fasciculations, weakness, and absent reflexes, I need to rule out motor neuron disease. Do you have any difficulty with speech, swallowing, or breathing, and have you noticed any muscle wasting in your limbs or tongue? REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG and NCS are normal, motor neuron disease and typical radiculopathy are unlikely, pointing toward a metabolic or systemic cause given your diabetes history. I will now request imaging to evaluate for cervical spine pathology and order specific blood work to check for diabetic neuropathy markers. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine REQUEST TEST: HbA1c

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a cervical syrinx, which explains your burning pain, weakness, and absent reflexes. I will now request images of the syrinx to better assess its extent and plan treatment. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The social history of inconsistent condom use raises suspicion for neurosyphilis, which can mimic or coexist with syringomyelia. I will request specific serological tests to rule out this infectious cause. REQUEST TEST: RPR REQUEST TEST: VDRL

speaker: Doctor
text: With syphilis ruled out and the MRI confirming a cervical syrinx likely secondary to your prior trauma, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
